title: MetaInfer → VibeQwen: from construction workflow to serving stack
summary: An author-reported experiment adapted MetaInfer and reused existing kernels to build a deployment-specific Qwen serving stack.
summary_cn: 一个改造智能体工作流、复用现有内核来构建专用执行栈的实验案例。
motivation: Target lower latency than a general engine for Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4 on one B200.
boundary: Model execution and serving integration, evaluated as deployed services; public VibeQwen engine source was not established.
reuse: vLLM/TensorRT-LLM kernels and references; MetaInfer is the adapted workflow, not VibeQwen source.
tradeoff: NVFP4 numerical differences were accepted if accuracy against BF16 was at least as good.
construction: Agent build/deploy/profile iterations: about one week, 1.7B mostly cached tokens and approximately 200 B200-hours.
ai_role: Disclosed: Claude Code with human steering, deployment access and measurement tools.
cost: Resource usage reported; fee estimates do not establish total development cost.
validation: Author-reported performance and accuracy checks; experimental, not production. No independent reproduction here.
maintenance: Long-term compatibility, regression coverage and maintenance effort were not established by the report.

title: Sol-Engine: compose and qualify model-specific optimizations
summary: An agent-oriented workflow assembles model-specific video execution paths from reusable optimizations and measured quality constraints.
summary_cn: 以智能体工作流组合模型专用优化，并以延迟和图像质量约束筛选配置。
motivation: The README identifies denoising-step redundancy, sparse interactions and repeated memory-bound operations as optimization opportunities.
boundary: The reviewed artifact is an optimized video codebase and configuration workflow, not a replacement for every serving layer.
reuse: Builds on SGLang multimodal_gen and existing model pipelines; combines cache, quantization, fusion, sparse attention and pruning.
tradeoff: Cache, sparsity and precision choices can change outputs; their effects must be separated from exact implementation changes.
construction: Documented workflow: executors explore configurations; an orchestrator checks, deduplicates and integrates results into reproducible run bundles.
ai_role: Intrinsic: the documented onboarding and optimization workflow uses coding agents; authored kernels remain reusable components.
cost: Total development tokens, GPU-hours and human maintenance costs are not disclosed in reviewed sources.
validation: Documented gates include LPIPS, visual review and checks that optimizations actually engaged; these are not equivalence proofs.
maintenance: Per-model hooks and backend combinations need qualification; long-term maintenance effort is not established.

title: Flash-MoE: SSD-streamed experts in a native prototype
summary: A fixed-model C/Metal prototype streams expert weights from SSD and controls the execution pipeline directly.
summary_cn: 围绕固定模型和苹果统一内存机器，直接组织 SSD 专家读取与 C/Metal 执行。
motivation: The stated target is running Qwen3.5-397B-A17B on a 48 GB MacBook despite weights exceeding RAM.
boundary: Owns model inference, routing, I/O and Metal execution; this is a narrow research prototype rather than a generic loader.
reuse: Uses Apple Metal, Accelerate BLAS, dispatch groups and the operating-system page cache alongside pretrained model weights.
tradeoff: The executable uses four experts although its source identifies ten active experts in the model; quantization adds another change.
construction: The author reports human–AI prototype construction; C/Metal sources expose the result. Detailed task division and iteration history are not established.
ai_role: Disclosed: the project describes a human-and-AI build. That statement does not establish autonomous correctness.
cost: The README reports a 24-hour human–AI prototype build; total lifecycle expenditure is not disclosed.
validation: The K=4 source and reported 2-bit JSON failures prevent treating headline speed as an equivalent top-10 baseline.
maintenance: Model geometry and packed files are specific; broader compatibility and sustained maintenance are not established.

title: DwarfStar: a deliberately narrow native execution stack
summary: A native stack integrates selected model paths, state management and local serving around consumer-hardware constraints.
summary_cn: 以少数模型和消费级硬件为边界，联合构建原生执行、状态管理与本地服务。
motivation: The author explicitly cites capable local models, expert quantization, compressed KV and fast SSDs as reasons for specialization.
boundary: Owns a narrow inference path plus CLI/server integration; it deliberately does not accept arbitrary GGUF models.
reuse: Its ds4.c inference path does not link GGML, but credits llama.cpp/GGML and retains or adapts quantization layouts, CPU logic and kernels.
tradeoff: Capacity depends on resident state, expert precision and SSD traffic; model coverage is intentionally selective.
construction: Public artifacts show native model paths and adapted lower-level code; the author describes humans guiding agent-assisted implementation, testing and debugging.
ai_role: Disclosed: strong coding-agent assistance, with humans leading ideas, testing and debugging.
cost: Total construction time, token usage and engineering expenditure are not disclosed in reviewed sources.
validation: The repository describes release QA and integrated tests; this survey did not reproduce its performance or numerical results.
maintenance: The author calls it beta and rapidly changing; supported models may be replaced as the project evolves.

title: Strata: tier experts around a gaming PC
summary: A Qwen-specific runtime combines GPU-resident work with CPU expert execution and explicit memory budgets.
summary_cn: 针对普通游戏电脑，将 GPU 热专家、CPU 冷专家和状态存储组合成模型专用运行时。
motivation: The stated goal is local Qwen3.8-Flash-Next inference on consumer NVIDIA or AMD PCs rather than server-sized GPU memory.
boundary: Integrates inference, memory policy and local APIs around one model family and qualified quantized layouts.
reuse: Credits GGML quantization formats, GPU dot/dequantization code, CPU expert kernels and the mtmd vision helper.
tradeoff: Eligible configurations enable route-tail-skip by default, dropping some missed experts; residency and CPU/GPU rounding also affect outputs.
construction: Public artifacts show a C++ runtime with CUDA/HIP and GGML-derived components. Development tools, task division and iteration history are not disclosed.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources. Compatibility with coding-agent clients is not evidence of AI-authored implementation.
cost: Development time, token expenditure and controlled construction-cost comparisons are not disclosed.
validation: Documented benchmark scenarios and source inspection expose configuration differences; no independent performance or quality reproduction was run.
maintenance: Device, quantization and skip-policy combinations require version-specific checks; maintenance effort is not disclosed.

title: NInfer: a native Qwen stack for one GPU
summary: Owns model execution, state and serving within a deliberately narrow checkpoint and GPU contract.
summary_cn: 围绕选定 Qwen 模型和 RTX 5090，自行组织模型计算、状态管理与请求服务。
motivation: The stated objective is maximum single-GPU performance for selected checkpoints; general model and device coverage is outside that target.
boundary: Native operators, model programs, state/KV management, scheduling and CLI/HTTP serving form one execution stack.
reuse: Retains pretrained weights, CUDA runtime, FFmpeg and HTTP/JSON/logging dependencies; owning execution does not imply a dependency-free system.
tradeoff: The upstream target is Linux with sm_120a, one resident model and startup-fixed execution lanes; it is not a general multi-device deployment contract.
construction: Public C++/CUDA modules and development contracts expose how components fit together. The actual development chronology and human–AI division of work are not disclosed.
ai_role: Not established. AI-assistance contribution policies and agent instruction files are not implementation-authorship evidence.
cost: Development effort and lifecycle costs are not disclosed; inference throughput does not establish construction economics.
validation: Published tests include independent operator oracles and opt-in real-engine integration checks. This survey did not execute them or reproduce performance.
maintenance: Explicit architecture and contribution boundaries constrain changes; artifact-version migration is documented, but sustained adaptation cost is unknown.

title: Iris: own the image pipeline in C
summary: A C image-generation pipeline replaces framework-level execution for selected architectures while retaining platform acceleration.
summary_cn: 用 C 接管选定图像模型的完整推理流程，同时复用系统数学库和 GPU 能力。
motivation: The README emphasizes minimal runtime dependencies and memory-mapped execution on machines with limited RAM.
boundary: Implements text encoding, diffusion-transformer execution and image decoding for selected FLUX and Z-Image variants.
reuse: Consumes existing model weights and safetensors; accelerated paths use system Metal/MPS and optional BLAS.
tradeoff: Native implementation narrows dependencies, but CPU fallbacks and different model variants do not have identical performance or quality.
construction: Public artifacts show architecture-specific C implementation and platform backends. Sources describe C/Python reference debugging, but not the full development sequence or task division.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources; disclosure from the author’s other projects must not be transferred to Iris.
cost: Construction time, AI-token spending and maintenance economics are not disclosed in reviewed sources.
validation: The repository describes reference-image checks and C/Python debugging comparisons; performance and output claims were not independently reproduced.
maintenance: New architectures need implementation and reference checks; the reviewed sources do not quantify that continuing effort.

title: TensorFold: qualify native paths by checkpoint and platform
summary: A Zig server admits explicit model–format–platform combinations and executes their native Metal or CUDA paths.
summary_cn: 以模型、权重格式和平台的资格表限定支持范围，再提供原生 Zig 服务与专用执行。
motivation: Documented objective: serve qualified language-model checkpoints directly from a binary without a Python or MLX serving installation.
boundary: Owns loading, tokenization, serving and execution for admitted combinations; experimental Living Weights is a separate model-changing feature.
reuse: Reuses existing model checkpoints, quantization encodings and platform GPU runtimes; reading an MLX format does not mean running MLX.
tradeoff: Packed formats and backend capabilities constrain fusion; a supported model name alone does not qualify every checkpoint.
construction: Public artifacts show native Zig model paths and format-aware readers. The authoring workflow and division of implementation work are not disclosed.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources; native code or compact packaging does not identify its authorship process.
cost: Development time, token/GPU expenditure and long-term engineering costs are not disclosed.
validation: The README provides qualification tables, golden-test commands and cache-state checks; this survey did not rerun them.
maintenance: Qualification is versioned and hardware-specific; adding readers or platforms creates additional compatibility obligations.

title: Halogen Flash: specialize a closed binary to one chip
summary: A distributed binary targets one Qwen family and AMD Strix Halo, with public deployment and quantization descriptions.
summary_cn: 以一个模型家族和一类芯片为边界发布专用二进制，公开部署与量化说明。
motivation: The README explicitly trades portability for model-and-chip specialization, targeting long local coding-agent sessions.
boundary: Public material exposes deployment and behavior; the core engine and complete tensor-level quantization choices are not publicly inspectable.
reuse: Uses pretrained weights and accepts selected llama.cpp GGUF files; underlying implementation reuse is not established by public documentation.
tradeoff: Mixed precision and narrow hardware support shape the result; repeatable binary benchmarks cannot substitute for source-level inspection.
construction: Documentation describes dedicated attention/expert kernels, separate state budgets and a paged n-gram lookup table.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources; serving agents does not establish that agents built the engine.
cost: Development time, token usage and engineering costs are not disclosed in reviewed sources.
validation: The publisher provides verification and benchmark modes; their numerical guarantees and performance were not independently reproduced here.
maintenance: Compatibility follows binary releases and supported hardware; maintenance effort and reproducible source builds are not established.

title: Magnitude: specialize kernels inside MLX execution
summary: The reviewed Metal path captures typed operations and constructs specialized fused kernels inside MLX’s execution machinery.
summary_cn: 在 MLX 执行体系内捕获带类型的运算，按数值契约与张量布局构造专用融合内核。
motivation: The README presents local, hardware-specific compilation and tuning for agent inference; historical framework bottlenecks are not established.
boundary: The inspected kernel layer owns planning and generated entry points, not a second device runtime or independent scheduler.
reuse: Retains MLX arrays, tracing, compilation and dependency management, combining upstream primitives with handwritten Metal implementations.
tradeoff: Encodings, shapes and numerical contracts restrict legal composition; unfamiliar operations and shapeless compilation retain upstream behavior.
construction: Capture operations, select compatible implementations, emit Metal entry points, then reconnect the transformed graph to native MLX compilation.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources; an engine for agents is not automatically an agent-generated engine.
cost: Total development effort and amortization of device-specific tuning are not disclosed in reviewed sources.
validation: Design documents define qualification obligations; inspecting compiler code does not prove every handwritten kernel satisfies them.
maintenance: The evidence covers inference-v2 Metal/MLX; other backends and continuing qualification costs remain outside this audit.

title: KTransformers: integrate CPU expert execution with GPU serving
summary: A specialized heterogeneous backend uses CPU capacity and instruction sets for MoE experts while retaining GPU serving components.
summary_cn: 将面向 CPU 指令集与 NUMA 的专家执行后端接入 GPU 服务路径。
motivation: The documented use case is large MoE inference with limited GPU resources and substantial CPU memory.
boundary: The reviewed kt-kernel path is an integrated backend; it is distinct from legacy injection examples and separate training features.
reuse: Reuses GPU serving integrations, model formats and libraries including a llamafile-based CPU backend, alongside AMX/AVX-specific implementations.
tradeoff: The useful partition depends on CPU ISA, NUMA placement, precision and communication costs; CPU capacity alone does not guarantee speed.
construction: The project documents kt-kernel implementations and serving integration. Its development iterations and division of work between people and tools are not established.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources. Supporting agent workloads does not disclose an AI development process.
cost: Hardware configurations are documented; controlled construction-time and maintenance-cost accounting is not disclosed.
validation: README support matrices and an AMX MoE implementation were inspected; benchmark and correctness claims were not independently reproduced.
maintenance: Kernel variants, weight formats and serving integrations evolve separately and require compatible versions.

title: Nunchaku: build execution around an SVDQuant artifact
summary: A low-bit diffusion backend co-designs packed weights and fused execution so the outlier-correction branch remains affordable.
summary_cn: 围绕 SVDQuant 权重与低秩修正分支，联合设计低比特布局和融合执行。
motivation: The documented problem is that an otherwise useful low-rank branch adds activation reads and writes that erode quantization gains.
boundary: Implements specialized diffusion-model execution components and integrations; it does not replace all text encoding, decoding or application layers.
reuse: Uses DeepCompressor-prepared checkpoints and existing PyTorch/Diffusers integrations; low-bit and low-rank CUDA kernels supply the specialized path.
tradeoff: Quantization changes numerical computation; reduced offloading, optional caching and checkpoint changes must be separated from kernel-level benefits.
construction: Source exposes custom CUDA operations through Python model adapters. The development chronology and division of automated and human work are not established.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources; model quantization and automatic kernels do not imply coding-agent authorship.
cost: Calibration and conversion are preparation work; developer effort and total construction economics are not disclosed.
validation: Public examples, quality results and kernels support inspection, but this survey did not independently reproduce image quality or speed.
maintenance: Support depends on checkpoint format, model adapters and CUDA/PyTorch compatibility; maintenance effort is not quantified.

title: ExLlamaV3: couple low-bit artifacts to a dedicated library
summary: A local-inference library couples EXL3 encoding, quantized state and qualified execution paths for consumer GPUs.
summary_cn: 将 EXL3 编码、低比特状态与专用执行路径配套，服务消费级 GPU 本地推理。
motivation: The README targets flexible quantization, parallel inference and large models with limited consumer-GPU resources.
boundary: Provides model execution and generation machinery; the recommended OpenAI-compatible server is the separate TabbyAPI project.
reuse: EXL3 builds on QTIP; the project uses PyTorch and credits FlashAttention, Marlin and vendored Flash Linear Attention kernels.
tradeoff: Weight/KV precision, model layout and decode geometry constrain optimized paths; quantized results are not the full-precision reference.
construction: Public artifacts provide a dedicated inference library and conversion tools. The development workflow is not disclosed; weight conversion is deployment preparation, not engine authorship evidence.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources. Automated conversion and dispatch do not identify the software’s development process.
cost: The README reports conversion in minutes to hours on a high-end consumer GPU, depending on model size; total engineering costs are unknown.
validation: Optimization documentation and quantized-cache code were inspected; conversion quality and end-to-end speed were not independently reproduced.
maintenance: Model support, kernel eligibility and PyTorch/CUDA/Triton versions create separate compatibility obligations.

title: Mirage MPK: compile an explicit graph into persistent execution
summary: A compiler/runtime turns an assembled LLM task graph into persistent GPU execution spanning computation and communication.
summary_cn: 将显式组装的 LLM 任务图编译为覆盖计算与通信的持久 GPU 执行程序。
motivation: The documented objective is reducing inference latency by moving model-wide execution into a single persistent megakernel.
boundary: This case covers the MPK branch and its supported task graph, not automatic support for arbitrary Hugging Face models.
reuse: Attaches existing PyTorch tensors, uses CUDA and NVSHMEM resources, and assembles supported fused operations rather than inventing model weights.
tradeoff: Graph coverage, tensor geometry and worker/scheduler allocation constrain generated programs; hardware resources must be budgeted explicitly.
construction: Define inputs, outputs and fused tasks, configure GPU workers, compile the graph and execute the resulting persistent program.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources; compiler automation is not itself evidence of coding-agent participation.
cost: End-to-end construction, tuning and maintenance costs are not disclosed in reviewed sources.
validation: Public demos and profiling interfaces expose execution; this survey inspected compiler/runtime boundaries without reproducing reported speedups.
maintenance: New models require supported task implementations and graph assembly; hardware changes require configuration and compatibility checks.
